title: Open Problem (constant c vs. |H|)
statement_text: For a planar graph $H$, find good bounds on $c=c(H)$ as a function of $|H|$ in the Erdős–Pósa bounding function $f(k)=ck\log(k+1)$ for $H$-models (that is, such that $\tau_H(G)\le f(\nu_H(G))$ for every graph $G$); in particular, determine whether $c$ could depend polynomially on $|H|$.
context_text: An $H$-model in a graph $G$ is a collection $\{M_x:x\in V(H)\}$ of vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of $G$ such that $M_x$ and $M_y$ are joined by an edge of $G$ for every edge $xy\in E(H)$ (so $G$ has an $H$-model if and only if $H$ is a minor of $G$); two models are disjoint if their vertex sets are. $\nu_H(G)$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint $H$-models in $G$, and $\tau_H(G)$ is the minimum size of a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G-X$ has no $H$-model. The Erdős–Pósa property holds for $H$-models with bounding function $f$ if $\tau_H(G)\le f(\nu_H(G))$ for every graph $G$; by Robertson and Seymour this holds for some $f$ if and only if $H$ is planar. Chekuri and Chuzhoy obtained $f(k)=ck\log^d(k+1)$ for a universal constant $d$, with $c$ depending polynomially on $|H|$ (using the Polynomial Grid Minor Theorem). The authors prove that for each planar $H$ there is $c=c(H)$ such that $f(k)=ck\log(k+1)$ works, which is best possible up to $c$ when $H$ contains a cycle (for forests an $O(k)$ bound is known). However, their constant $c$ is enormous and not even known to be computable, since the proof uses a non-constructive result of Fomin, Lokshtanov, Misra and Saurabh on minor-minimal graphs with $\tau_H(G)=t$.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled environment: "Finding good bounds on c as a function of |H| is left as an open problem, in particular it would be interesting to determine whether c could depend polynomially on |H|."
paper_title: A tight Erdős-Pósa function for planar minors
